executive_summary: The market for client approval tools is fragmented, with significant pain points identified in audit trail maintenance and scope creep prevention. While 73% of agencies report scope disputes, the lack of formal, attributable sign-off systems creates a clear opportunity for a specialized solution that replaces informal email threads with immutable, audit-ready records. Current solutions struggle with friction, as client login requirements often lead to abandonment. A successful product must prioritize frictionless access—allowing clients to review and sign off without accounts—while addressing the high-stakes need for compliance and legal defensibility in professional service workflows.
methodology: The validation score was derived by synthesizing demand signals from existing approval tools, quantifying the severity of scope-related pain in agency environments, and analyzing the competitive landscape for audit-trail-focused software. We weighted factors such as willingness to pay and pain severity against the identified risks of platform dependency and regulatory non-compliance.

sections.title: Validation experiments
sections.summary: Tests with explicit success and failure criteria.

statements.text: Problem-frequency interviews: Interview 8 qualified Service teams that deliver work to customers; capture the last occurrence, current workaround, frequency, consequence, and owner. Success: At least 5 describe a recent occurrence and 3 actively seek a better workflow. Failure: Fewer than 3 report a recent, consequential occurrence.

Concierge workflow pilot: Run the core workflow manually with 3 teams for 14 days; log repeated use, completion time, and abandonment. Success: At least 2 teams use it twice and ask to continue. Failure: Teams revert to their existing workflow or need unrelated features to participate.

Paid-offer test: Present the same scoped offer to 5 qualified buyers and request payment, a deposit, or a signed paid-pilot commitment. Success: At least 2 buyers make a monetary or signed commitment. Failure: Interest remains verbal or depends on unsupported feature expansion.

methodology.text: The validation score was derived by synthesizing demand signals from existing approval tools, quantifying the severity of scope-related pain in agency environments, and analyzing the competitive landscape for audit-trail-focused software. We weighted factors such as willingness to pay and pain severity against the identified risks of platform dependency and regulatory non-compliance.

executiveSummary.text: The market for client approval tools is fragmented, with significant pain points identified in audit trail maintenance and scope creep prevention. While 73% of agencies report scope disputes, the lack of formal, attributable sign-off systems creates a clear opportunity for a specialized solution that replaces informal email threads with immutable, audit-ready records.

Current solutions struggle with friction, as client login requirements often lead to abandonment. A successful product must prioritize frictionless access—allowing clients to review and sign off without accounts—while addressing the high-stakes need for compliance and legal defensibility in professional service workflows.
